The design system spec holds records: components, patterns, guidelines, and examples. A component
is a technology-neutral contract (anatomy, parameters, states, rules, tokens), not framework code.
Implement it in whatever technology the project uses.

- Use the `taproot` CLI when you have a terminal, and the `taproot` MCP server when you
  do not. Run the CLI from an installed copy, never an `npx` download per call: in this repository,
  `node packages/spec/bin/taproot.js`; in a project that depends on the package,
  `node_modules/.bin/taproot`.
- Start with `search` to choose a component, then `get` it and follow its links: `alternative` for
  when it is the wrong choice, `follows` for the patterns and guidelines it applies, `examples` for
  worked usage.
- Use `rules` to review work, and cite each rule by its address (for example
  `component.button#label-describes-result`) with its level (MUST, SHOULD, MAY). A component's
  rules include those of the patterns and guidelines it follows, at their own addresses (for
  example `pattern.form-field#error-blocks-submit`).
- Use `tokens` for the design tokens a component part uses in a variant or state. Add `--resolve`
  (MCP: `resolve`) for values. Use `format` for what records do not repeat: the system-wide
  constants, such as border width and focus-ring width and offset, with their tokens.
- Before writing code, `get` the component with the implementation for your technology:
  `--impl web` for web components, `--impl react` for React (MCP: `implementation`). It gives the
  package, what to import, and the attribute or prop that implements each parameter. Never derive
  those names from parameter names. Once per project, read `setup --impl <name>` (MCP: `setup`)
  for what every component shares: installing the package, loading its styles, and fonts.
- Components style only themselves. Before building a page, `get guideline.page-setup` for the
  page's base font, text color, background, and heading recipes, and load the base stylesheet it
  names when your technology has one.
- For several lookups, run them in one `batch` with the CLI (for example
  `taproot batch --command "get button --impl web" --command "tokens button"`), or make the
  tool calls in parallel on the MCP server.

$ taproot setup --impl web
# Web components setup

What every web component needs, once per project. Each component's own file in this folder maps its
API; `taproot setup --impl web` prints this one.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @taproot-ds/web-components @taproot-ds/tokens
```

## Load the styles

Load the token stylesheet once, at the application root, before any component renders. Without it,
the components have no colors, spacing, or type. The optional base stylesheet styles the page
around them: the base font, text color, background, and a type recipe for each heading level
(`guideline.page-setup`). The components style only themselves.

```js
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/css";
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/base"; // optional page defaults
```

Without a bundler, link the files from the tokens package instead:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/tokens.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/base.css" />
```

The components read semantic tokens directly, so they follow the active theme. With no
`data-theme` on the root element, the theme follows the system preference; `data-theme="light"` or
`"dark"` overrides it. The tokens a component reads are not a customization API.

## Fonts

The font tokens name Lora, Source Sans 3, and JetBrains Mono, with system fallbacks. The packages do
not ship the font files. The tokens package's readme has the links to load them.

## Register the elements

Import the package root once to register every element under its `ds-` tag:

```js
import "@taproot-ds/web-components";
```

Or import one component's module and call its define function, as each component's Import section
shows. A define function takes another tag name when `ds-` names collide.

The modules are standard ES modules with no runtime dependencies. Without a bundler, map the bare
package names with an import map, or import the files under `node_modules/@taproot-ds/web-components/src/`.

$ taproot get guideline.page-setup
# Page setup

Set the page's base font, text color, background, and heading type from semantic tokens, because components style only themselves.

The components style only themselves. The page around them, the text between them, and the
headings above them get no style from any component. Without these defaults, components look right
while the page around them falls back to the platform's serif font and plain white, and nothing
reports the gap.

## What the page sets

| Page element | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Background | `semantic.color.background.default` | The page itself. Raised areas use `semantic.color.background.surface`. |
| Base text | `semantic.typography.body.md` | Font family, size, weight, line height, and letter spacing. |
| Text color | `semantic.color.foreground.default` | Supporting text uses `semantic.color.foreground.muted`. |
| Small print | `semantic.typography.body.sm` | Captions and fine print. |
| Page title (level 1) | `semantic.typography.heading.lg` | One per page. |
| Section heading (level 2) | `semantic.typography.heading.md` | |
| Subsection heading (level 3) | `semantic.typography.heading.sm` | The recipe Card uses for its title. |
| Deeper headings (levels 4 to 6) | `semantic.typography.title` | The bold sans title Alert and Dialog use. |
| Code | `semantic.typography.code.md` | Inline code and code blocks. |
| Eyebrow above a heading | `semantic.typography.eyebrow` | A short category line, not a heading. |

A typography token such as `semantic.typography.body.md` is a recipe: it groups a font family,
size, weight, line height, and letter spacing, and each is its own token
(`semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily`). Set all five together. Mixing parts of two recipes
produces a size and line height that were never designed together.

For the values in each theme, read the token package, or resolve a component that uses the
recipe, such as `taproot tokens card --part title --resolve`.

## Token names in your technology

A token reference such as `semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily` is technology-neutral. Each
technology's token package publishes it under its own name, and that package says how. In the web
package, a reference becomes a CSS custom property: prefix `--ds-`, join the segments with hyphens,
and turn camel case into hyphenated words, so the reference above is
`--ds-semantic-typography-body-md-font-family`. Check a name against the package's stylesheet
before you rely on it (`no-guessed-names`).

## Fonts

The font tokens name the system's typefaces with fallbacks. The token package does not ship the
font files. Load the typefaces the way your platform does, before the page renders; the token
package's readme lists them and gives the web links to load them. Without them, the fallbacks keep the page readable but it does not
look like the system.

## Theme

The token package follows the reader's light or dark preference, and lets the page choose one
instead. Set the theme at the root of the page so the background, the base text, and every
component change together. A part of the page that sets its own colors without semantic tokens
does not change with them.

## Spacing and layout

Lay out the page with the spacing primitives, `primitives.space.*`, and put product layout
between components rather than inside them (`guideline.compose-or-propose`). The system has no
grid, container, or page template component; compose those in product code.

## Rules

### Behavior

- **MUST** load-tokens: Load the token package once, at the root of the page, before any component renders. Without it, components have no colors, spacing, or type.
- **MUST** page-base-text: The page's base text uses the body recipe, `semantic.typography.body.md`, in `semantic.color.foreground.default`. Text the components do not draw would otherwise fall back to the platform's default font and color.
- **MUST** page-background: The page background is `semantic.color.background.default`, so it follows the active theme with the components on it.
- **SHOULD** heading-recipes: Each heading level uses a heading recipe: the page title `semantic.typography.heading.lg`, section headings `semantic.typography.heading.md`, subsection headings `semantic.typography.heading.sm`, and deeper levels `semantic.typography.title`. Choose the level by the document outline, and the recipe by the level.
- **SHOULD** base-stylesheet: Where the token package offers a base stylesheet for your technology, load it rather than writing the page defaults by hand. It applies these rules with names that are already right. `taproot setup --impl <name>` names it for each implementation.
- **MUST** no-guessed-names: Take each token's name in your technology from the token package or a lookup, never from a guess. A misspelled token name fails silently and the platform default shows instead.

## Links

### related

- [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility)
- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)

# Text area

Use Text area to collect multiple lines of text with a label, hint, and error.

Collects multiple lines of text and associates a label, optional hint, and optional error with the control.

## When to use

- Collect comments, descriptions, or messages that may span several lines.
- Pair with Button when the value should be submitted.

## When not to use

- Collect a short single-line value. Use [Text field](component.text-field) instead. Text field keeps short values compact.
- Author rich formatted content. Instead: Rich text editor. Text area collects plain text.

## Anatomy

Triggers an action or submits or resets a form. ## When to use - Trigger an action in the current view. - Submit or reset a form. ## When not to use - Navigate to another location. Use [Link](component.link) instead. A link carries a destination that people can open, copy, or share. - Display status or metadata. Use [Badge](component.badge) instead. Button communicates an available action. ## Anatomy | Part | Role | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | control | interactive-surface | Interactive control. | | content | label | Action label with an optional decorative icon. | ## Parameters | Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | variant | enum | `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `destructive` | `primary` | | | size | enum | `small`, `medium` | `medium` | | | action | enum | `activate`, `submit`, `reset` | `activate` | | | disabled | boolean | | `false` | | | fullWidth | boolean | | `false` | Fills the available inline size. | | accessibleName | string | | | Accessible name when visible content is insufficient. | `variant` values: - `primary`: Highest-emphasis action. Example: Save changes Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#primary) - `secondary`: Supporting action. Example: Cancel Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#secondary) - `tertiary`: Low-emphasis action. Example: View details Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#tertiary) - `destructive`: Destructive or difficult-to-reverse action. Example: Delete project Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#destructive) `size` values: - `small`: Small button. - `medium`: Medium button. `action` values: - `activate`: Triggers an action. - `submit`: Submits the associated form. - `reset`: Resets the associated form. ## Events - `activate`: Requests the action represented by the button. ## States `disabled`, `pressed`, `hover`, `focus`, `default` ## Preferences - `reducedMotion`: `reduce` ## Rules Includes the rules of guideline.accessibility, which this component follows. Cite each rule by the address shown. ### Content - **MUST** label-describes-result: Use a concise label that describes the result. - Do: Save changes; Delete account - Avoid: Click here - **MUST** destructive-for-risky-actions: Use the destructive variant only for destructive or difficult-to-reverse actions. - **SHOULD** explain-disabled: When the context does not say why an action is disabled, say why near it. - **SHOULD** follow-action-hierarchy: Apply the action hierarchy pattern when several actions appear together. - See: pattern.action-hierarchy#assign-emphasis ### Behavior - **MUST** disabled-prevents-activation: Disabled prevents activation. - **SHOULD** explicit-form-action: In a form, set action to submit or reset when the button should submit or reset. The default activate does neither. - **SHOULD** form-submit-reset: Submit submits the button's form, and reset restores that form's initial values. - Applies when: The button belongs to a form. - **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-a-control: The component is not focusable and does not activate. - Applies when: The component is not interactive. ### Accessibility - **MUST** icon-accessible-name: Icon-only buttons have an accessible name. - **MUST** forced-colors: Under forced colors, emphasis stays visible: primary and destructive are filled, secondary is outlined, and tertiary is text alone. A disabled button stays distinguishable from an enabled one. - Extends: guideline.accessibility#forced-colors - **MUST** guideline.accessibility#visible-focus: Keyboard focus is visibly indicated on every focusable part, in every variant and state. - Applies when: A part of the component takes keyboard focus. - **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-color-alone: Meaning never depends on color alone. Text, shape, or position carries it too. ## Accessibility - Role: Button - Name: Required from visible content or accessibleName. | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | Tab | Move focus to or from the button. | | Enter | Activate. | | Space | Activate. | ## Rationale - **Button reads semantic tokens directly and has no component-token namespace.** Its component tokens only restated the semantic tier, so they added names without adding a customization boundary (tokens ADR 0003). ## Links ### alternative - [Badge](component.badge) — Display status or metadata. Button communicates an available action. - [Link](component.link) — Navigate to another location. A link carries a destination that people can open, copy, or share. ### alternative-to - [Avatar](component.avatar) — Open a profile or account menu by pressing the avatar. Avatar is not a control. Place it inside a Button or a Link, which give the action its role, focus, and accessible name. - [Badge](component.badge) — Trigger an action in the current view. Badge is not interactive and does not communicate an available action. - [Card](component.card) — Make a large target that only triggers one action or navigates, with no content of its own. A control styled as a card hides its role. Use Button for an action, or Link for navigation, and let the card hold content. - [Checkbox](component.checkbox) — Trigger an action by itself. Checkbox records a choice. - [Icon](component.icon) — Trigger an action with an icon alone. Icon is not a control. A button with an icon and an accessible name gives the action semantics and focus. - [Link](component.link) — Trigger an action or submit a form. Buttons provide action semantics and form behavior. - [Text field](component.text-field) — Trigger an action by itself. Text field collects a value. ### composes - [Icon](component.icon) ### follows - [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility) - [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#assign-emphasis) - `parameters.variant.destructive` → [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#destructive) - `parameters.variant.primary` → [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#primary) - `parameters.variant.secondary` → [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#secondary) - `parameters.variant.tertiary` → [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#tertiary) ### related - [Spinner](component.spinner) - [Tooltip](component.tooltip) - [Settings action hierarchy](example.action-hierarchy.settings) - [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose) ### used-in - [Alert](component.alert) - [Dialog](component.dialog) ## Web implementation - Package: `@taproot-ds/web-components` - Element: `` ### Import ```js import { defineButton } from "@taproot-ds/web-components/button"; defineButton(); ``` ### Usage ```html Save changes ``` ### API | Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `variant` | attribute | parameter `variant` | `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `destructive` | | | `size` | attribute | parameter `size` | `small`, `medium` | | | `type` | attribute | parameter `action` | `activate` → `button`, `submit`, `reset` | | | `disabled` | attribute | parameter `disabled` | boolean | | | `full-width` | attribute | parameter `fullWidth` | boolean | Fills the available inline size. | | `aria-label` | attribute | parameter `accessibleName` | string | Accessible name when visible content is insufficient. | | `form` | property | | `HTMLFormElement \| null` | The associated form, including association across the shadow boundary. | | `click` | event | event `activate` | | Requests the action represented by the button. | A row with no Implements entry is specific to this implementation, not part of the spec. ### Forms Button defaults to `type="button"`. Set the type when it participates in a form: ```html
Cancel Save changes
``` Use `type="reset"` only when restoring every form control to its initial value is the intended behavior. ### Styles Do not recreate Button states with product CSS. Use the published variants and sizes first. Treat `::part(button)` as an escape hatch that requires a specific product need and design review. ### Icons Mark a decorative icon hidden from assistive technology. Provide `aria-label` when an icon is the only visible content. ### Why `aria-label` and not `label` Button maps `accessibleName` to `aria-label`, while Icon, Spinner, and Tabs map it to `label`. The difference is deliberate. `aria-label` is the attribute people already put on an icon-only button, and Button only passes it to the native button inside, so it keeps its standard meaning. The other three use `label` because their name does more than name: Icon is hidden from assistive technology without one, Spinner falls back to "Loading", and Tabs names the tab list inside it rather than the host. They set the name through `ElementInternals` or on that inner element, so the host never gains `aria-*` attributes. Renaming either side would break published markup. Tokens: 50 bindings, left out here. Run `taproot tokens component.button` to filter them by part, condition, or property. Setup: install, styles, and fonts are the same for every component. Run `taproot setup --impl web` once per project. $ taproot tokens --help taproot tokens [--part

74:## Fonts
76:The design system uses three typefaces, each mapped to a font token:
80:| `--ds-primitives-font-display` | Lora           | Headings, card titles, logotype  |
81:| `--ds-primitives-font-sans`    | Source Sans 3  | Body text, UI labels, buttons    |
82:| `--ds-primitives-font-mono`    | JetBrains Mono | Code, token values, numeric data |
84:Each token includes a system fallback stack, so the UI remains readable if Google Fonts fails to load. To use the intended typefaces, add the following `<link>` tags to your document `<head>` **before** the tokens stylesheet:
87:<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />
88:<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />
90:  href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Lora:ital,wght@0,400..700;1,400..700&family=Source+Sans+3:wght@300..900&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;600&display=swap"
95:The `display=swap` parameter ensures text renders immediately in the fallback font while the custom fonts load, avoiding invisible text during page load.
97:If you are using a bundler with a `<head>` injection plugin (e.g. Vite's `vite-plugin-html`) or a framework like Next.js, load the fonts using your framework's preferred font mechanism instead of a raw `<link>` tag.
